title: Spanish Chicken Croquetas with Creamy Béchamel
summary: Creamy chicken béchamel is chilled, shaped and coated in crumbs before frying to a golden crisp, giving warm, molten croquetas inside.
equipment: second frying pan or sauté pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
plain flour, sifted, plus extra for dusting
sunflower or mild olive oil, for frying

steps.title: Cook Chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan on medium, salt the chicken and cook until it reaches 74°C, about 10 minutes, then cool, chop and grind finely in a food processor.

steps.title: Soften Onion
steps.text: Melt the butter in a second pan on medium and cook the finely chopped onion gently until soft and clear but not coloured, about 12 minutes.

steps.title: Heat Milk
steps.text: Bring the milk to a simmer in a saucepan, season with salt, pepper and nutmeg, then cover and keep hot.

steps.title: Make Roux
steps.text: Sift the flour over the onion and stir constantly for 2 minutes until it forms a moist ball.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Spread the mixture out and gradually stir in the hot milk until thick, creamy and no longer sticky, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: On low heat fold in the ground chicken and cook for 2 minutes until the mixture holds together, then spread in a bowl, cool, cover and chill for several hours until firm.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: On a floured board, shape the mixture into 5-6 cm logs about 2.5 cm thick and roll lightly in flour.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Dip each log in beaten egg, then in breadcrumbs, to coat fully.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 2 cm oil in a pan over medium-high, lower to medium-low and fry in small batches, turning, until golden and hot and creamy inside, about 2 minutes; drain on paper and serve hot.

tips: Chill the chicken mixture for several hours, or even overnight, so it's firm enough to shape without falling apart.
Fry in small batches and keep the oil at a steady temperature so the coating turns golden before the inside overheats.
Make sure the chicken reaches 74°C when first cooking it, for safe, fully cooked meat.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Shape and chill the mixture up to a day ahead; once fried, croquetas are best eaten hot and freshly cooked rather than kept. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
